title: Tracxn Q2 Loss Narrows 26% YoY To ₹4.1 Cr, Revenue Stays Flat
title_bn: ট্র্যাক্সন দ্বিতীয় প্রান্তিকে ২৬ শতাংশ হ্রাস পেয়ে ৪.১ কোটি টাকা হয়েছে।
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Listed private market intelligence platform Tracxn Technologies reported a 25.8% decline in its net loss to ₹4.1 Cr in the…
paragraph1: Listed private market intelligence platform Tracxn Technologies reported a 25.8% decline in its net loss to ₹4.1 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 (Q2 FY27) from ₹5.6 Cr, helped by a lower tax charge. Sequentially, its loss widened 37.1% from ₹3 Cr. Operating revenue remained largely flat, rising 0.3% to ₹21.3 Cr from ₹21.2 Cr. The top line increased 1.1% from ₹21.1 Cr in the preceding quarter. The narrower YoY net loss reflects a change in tax expenses.
paragraph2: Tracxn incurred a ₹6.2 Cr tax charge in Q2 FY26, compared with a ₹52 Lakh tax credit in the quarter under review. Before tax, the company swung to a loss of ₹4.6 Cr from a profit of ₹62.4 Lakh a year earlier. Its pre-tax loss stood at ₹2.8 Cr in Q1 FY27. The Bengaluru-based company provides private-company data and software to venture capital firms, private equity firms, investment banks, and corporate teams. Total income, including other income and gains, stood at ₹22.7 Cr, compared with ₹22.5 Cr in Q2 FY26 and ₹22.6 Cr in the preceding quarter. Tracxn’s total expenses rose 25% YoY to ₹27.3 Cr from ₹21.
paragraph3: 9 Cr. Sequentially, expenses increased 7.7% from ₹25.4 Cr. For the first half of FY27, operating revenue declined marginally to ₹42.4 Cr from ₹42.5 Cr in the corresponding period last fiscal. Total expenses increased 21.7% YoY to ₹52.7 Cr from ₹43.3 Cr, while net loss widened 60.6% to ₹7.1 Cr from ₹4.4 Cr.
paragraph4: Tracxn reported a net cash outflow of ₹6 Cr from operating activities in H1 FY27, against an inflow of ₹1 Cr a year earlier. India Growth Offsets Overseas Decline India accounted for 53% of Tracxn’s Q2 FY27 revenue, with domestic revenue growing 6.9% sequentially to ₹11.3 Cr. The company said this represented an annualised growth run rate of nearly 30%. International revenue declined 4.8% sequentially to ₹10 Cr, accounting for the remaining 47%. Tracxn said investments in data and sales capabilities in India over the past two to three years were driving domestic growth. It is now making similar investments across its international business units, which it expects to support growth over the coming quarters. Its strategy involves creating specialised teams for customer segments, expanding relevant datasets and product capabilities, and then scaling sales teams. For instance, monthly new customer wins in its India investment banking business increased from nine to 13 during FY26 and reached 20 in Q1 FY27. It is targeting 30 monthly wins. Tracxn plans to expand the sales team responsible for closing deals from 34 members in December 2025 to around 60 by December 2026. Of these planned positions, 56 had been filled by September.
paragraph5: Sales and marketing teams accounted for 30% of its total headcount in Q2 FY27, up from 25% a year earlier. AI And Data Expansion Tracxn has introduced Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors that allow paid users to access its proprietary company intelligence through AI tools including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Cursor. It has also introduced an AI assistant that lets users query its database in plain English, alongside ready-to-use investor agents for tasks including due diligence, competitive benchmarking, sector research, and startup scouting. More workflows are planned. On data coverage, Tracxn said its database contained detailed financials for more than 7.5 Mn companies across over 20 countries, while its global legal entity database covered 66 Mn entities. The company is also using Tracxn Lite, which offers limited platform access, to attract potential paying customers. It reported 3.49 Lakh cumulative sign-ups and 17.1 Mn organic visits during Q2 FY27. Customer accounts increased 13% YoY to 2,419, while users grew 16% to 6,854. Tracxn said it expects annual cost growth to moderate to low single digits after its current investment phase, supported by AI-led reductions in data production costs. It expects this to help it return to profitability.

author: TechPulse
excerpt: Designed for CPUs, GPUs, and other components without an integrated heat spreader, the PhaseSheet PTM Pro is reusable, electrically non-conductive, and less susceptible to the pump-out effect associated with traditional thermal paste.
paragraph1: Thermal Grizzly has announced the PhaseSheet PTM Pro, an improved version of its popular phase-changing thermal pad.
paragraph2: According to the manufacturer, the new thermal pad offers increased thermal conductivity alongside a redesigned carrier film that makes the PhaseSheet PTM Pro easier to handle and install.
paragraph3: While this may seem like a relatively minor change, the new carrier film is designed to peel away more easily from both sides, reducing the risk of tearing the sheet during installation.

author: TechPulse
excerpt: As DRAM and 3D NAND are about to adopt all-new technologies, custom types of memory are about to become mainstream as AI developers face limitations with current solutions.
paragraph1: Last month, Micron disclosed its DRAM and NAND memory roadmaps for the next several years, revealing plans to use wafer bonding, new materials that enable making NAND cells smaller, High-NA EUV lithography, and detailing its moves toward 3D DRAM.
paragraph2: Perhaps the most revealing part of Micron's story is that the company plans to expand its portfolio of custom DRAM and NAND products as AI developers increasingly require memory and storage solutions optimized for their unique processor architectures and specific workloads.

title_bn: এখন আপগ্রাড ১.০২ কোটি টাকার বেশি বেতনের জন্য বিরা ৯১-এর বিরুদ্ধে দেউলিয়া আবেদন দায়ের করেছে।
author: TechPulse
excerpt: upGrad has filed an insolvency petition against B9 Beverages Ltd, the maker of Bira91 beer, over alleged unpaid dues of…
paragraph1: SUMMARYupGrad has filed an insolvency petition against Bira 91 parent B9 Beverages over alleged unpaid dues of ₹1.02 Cr The petition adds to the mounting creditor pressure on B9 Beverages as it attempts to restructure its business and revive operations The petition was filed under Section 9 of the IBC on October 22, while the brewer is also facing an ₹11.77 Cr claim from glassmaker HNGIL upGrad has filed an insolvency petition against B9 Beverages Ltd, the maker of Bira91 beer, over alleged unpaid dues of ₹1.02 Cr, adding to the financial and legal challenges facing the brewer. The petition, filed under Section 9 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016, was submitted to the Delhi bench of the NCLT on October 22, as per documents reviewed by Moneycontrol. upGrad has named B9 Beverages as the corporate debtor and sought the initiation of the corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) to recover the outstanding amount. The petition does not disclose the nature of services provided by upGrad to the beverage maker. Inc42 has reached out to upGrad and Anicut Capital for a comment on the development.
paragraph2: The story will be updated on receiving a response. The filing comes amid mounting liabilities and creditor disputes at B9 Beverages, which is facing insolvency-related action from multiple creditors. In September, the NCLT directed B9 Beverages and its creditors to explore a settlement through mediation in connection with multiple insolvency proceedings. The tribunal also restrained the brewer from disposing of its assets while discussions were underway. The company has also faced action from glass manufacturer Hindusthan National Glass & Industries Ltd (HNGIL), which sought to recover ₹11.8 Cr in alleged unpaid dues. HNGIL issued a demand notice under Section 8 of the IBC over customised glass bottles manufactured against confirmed purchase orders but allegedly not collected by the brewer. The glassmaker claimed that more than 51 Lakh bottles worth over ₹7 Cr remained stored at its facilities, despite it encashing bank guarantees worth ₹3.
paragraph3: 91 Cr. The latest development comes as the startup attempts to restructure its business amid a prolonged financial crisis. In July, founder Ankur Jain stepped down from the company’s board and relinquished executive control and ownership following a dispute with investors and lenders. VC firm Anicut Capital, one of Bira’s key lenders, subsequently took control of Jain and his family’s stake in the company, as per reports. Anicut had extended loans to B9 Beverages between 2017 and 2022, secured against the promoter family’s stake. The brewer is now expected to be recapitalised by existing investors and lenders under a revival plan aimed at clearing statutory, employee and vendor dues and restarting operations. Founded by Jain in 2015, Bira 91 raised more than $200 Mn from investors. Its annual revenue crossed $100 Mn in FY23.
paragraph4: Its shareholders include Peak XV Partners, Sofina and Japan-based Kirin Holdings. Anicut Capital and Hero Corporate Services’ family office are among its key lenders. Its troubles began after it converted into a public company, triggering fresh excise approval requirements across multiple states. This disrupted the production and sales of the beer. The company subsequently wrote off inventory worth around ₹80 Cr and fell behind on vendor payments. The company eventually paused its packaged beer business amid a prolonged funding crunch, mounting vendor liabilities and difficulties in meeting employee and statutory obligations. The company reported a net loss of ₹748 Cr in FY24, with accumulated losses of ₹2,117.9 Cr.
paragraph5: Its auditor also warned that current liabilities exceeded assets by ₹487 Cr as of March 2024. Under Section 9 of the IBC, an operational creditor can approach the NCLT to initiate insolvency proceedings after serving a demand notice and meeting the prescribed statutory conditions. However, filing a petition does not automatically trigger insolvency proceedings. The NCLT will examine the application to determine whether the requirements for admission have been met.

bangla_paragraph4: Its shareholders include Peak XV Partners, Sofina and Japan-based Kirin Holdings. Anicut Capital and Hero Corporate Services’ family office are among its key lenders. Its troubles began after it converted into a public company, triggering fresh excise approval requirements across multiple states. This disrupted the production and sales of the beer. The company subsequently wrote off inventory worth around ₹80 Cr and fell behind on vendor payments. The company eventually paused its packaged beer business amid a prolonged funding crunch, mounting vendor liabilities and difficulties in meeting employee and statutory obligations. The company reported a net loss of ₹748 Cr in FY24, with accumulated losses of ₹2,117.9 Cr.

title_bn: পিএইচপি দুর্বলতা পোস্ট-মর্টেম বাগ প্রকাশ করে দুই বছর আগে পরিচিত ছিল  রক্ষণাবেক্ষণের একটি ছোট দল এটি প্রকাশ্যে প্রকাশের আগে সমস্যা সম্পর্কে জানত, কারণ নতুন পিএইਚপি 2 শেল চেইনড এক্সপ্লোয়াইট সার্ভারগুলি ধ্বংস করে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: PHP has a harvest season to remember — AI-automated bug hunting reaps what years of technical debt have sown.
paragraph1: (Image credit: Getty Images) The phrase "when it rains, it pours" applies both to weather and computer security, as proven the week of October 19, 2026, when OpenAI's GPT 5.6-Sol discovered critical vulnerabilities in the open-source programming language PHP. As published in a post-mortem, a small team of maintainers knew of the issue two years ago.
paragraph2: Security experts had warned for decades about mounting technical debt, as agentic AI exponentially sped up vulnerability scanning, to the point that the usual 90-day disclosure window for security exploits became pointless. PHP, one of the internet's ubiquitous software packages, was unlucky enough to in the crosshairs of bug-hunting AI agents.PHP hosts around 70% of websites on the internet, and the vulnerability allows for remote code execution with enough attacker knowledge.
paragraph3: That combination is enough to sound alarms, but the situation got worse once the collective internet realized that, at the time, 73% of PHP installations online were running end-of-life versions with no active support — eliciting face-palms from many techies, and an exasperated sigh from anyone familiar with the ecosystem, myself included. So ultimately the problem wasn't really the vulnerability, but the general complacency. Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware.
paragraph4: He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

title: PhysicsWallah Returns To The Black In Q2, Posts A Profit of ₹143.6 Cr

author: TechPulse
excerpt: Edtech major PhysicsWallah (PW) reported a consolidated net profit of ₹143.6 Cr in the second quarter (Q2) of the fiscal…
paragraph1: SUMMARYPhysicsWallah (PW) posted a consolidated net profit of ₹143.6 Cr in Q2 FY27, over double from ₹69.7 Cr profit registered in the year-ago quarter Total expenses stood at ₹1,105.4 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 10.6% from ₹999.6 Cr in the previous year Operating revenue rose 18.2% to ₹1,242.3 Cr from ₹1,051.3 Cr in the year-ago period. On a sequential basis, the company’s top line increased 15% to ₹918.8 Cr Edtech major PhysicsWallah (PW) reported a consolidated net profit of ₹143.6 Cr in the second quarter (Q2) of the fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27), up 106% from ₹69.7 Cr in the year-ago quarter. In contrast, the listed company had posted a loss of ₹88.3 Cr in the preceding quarter.
paragraph2: Meanwhile, operating revenue rose 18.2% to ₹1,242.3 Cr in the quarter under review from ₹1,051.3 Cr in Q2 FY26. On a sequential basis, the company’s top line also jumped 18.3% from ₹1,050.3 Cr in Q1 FY27. Including other income of ₹92.4 Cr, PhysicsWallah’s total income stood at ₹1,334.6 Cr in the quarter under review. In line with the top line, PW’s total expenses also rose 10.6% to ₹1,105.4 Cr in Q2 FY27 as against ₹999.6 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Employee benefit expenses, its largest cost centre, also rose 10.
paragraph3: 4% to ₹522.4 Cr from ₹473.1 Cr in the year-ago period. In its investor presentation, PW also noted that its EBITDA stood at ₹348 Cr in the quarter under review, up 52.6% from ₹228 Cr in Q2 FY26. Meanwhile, EBITDA margin improved to 28% from 21.7% in Q2 FY26. During the quarter, Physicswallah also reported a profit of ₹1.3 Cr from discontinued operations. Its subsidiary Finz Finance discontinued its lending business and transferred its loan portfolio to Auxilo Finserve for ₹95.8 Cr in October this year. PhysicsWallah’s Omnichannel Engine The online business accounted for the biggest chunk of PW’s top line in Q2 FY27. The vertical generated a revenue of ₹693.5 Cr during the quarter, up 26.4% from ₹548.
paragraph4: 7 Cr in Q2 FY26. On the other hand, the offline segment reported a revenue of ₹540.9 Cr, marking a 9% YoY increase from ₹496.1 Cr. On the operational front, the listed edtech major said that it operated 370 offline centres at the end of September 2026. Meanwhile, unique online enrolments grew 12.9% YoY to 15 Lakh in Q2 FY27. However, the quarter was not without its challenges. During the earnings call, the management said that the delayed NEET exam cycle slowed enrolments and collections, impacting both online and offline verticals. However, the offline business was impacted more. PW now expects collections to spill into Q3 FY27, while anticipating stronger recovery in the next academic session. Noting that NEET accounts for only about 15% of online revenue, the management noted that the hit from the subdued performance of the medical exam vertical was largely offset by other categories. To further offset the gap, PW said that it is increasing non-NEET enrolments as well as launching full-length crash courses and a 360-degree tracker product. PW’s Next Growth Bet In the earnings call, PhysicsWallah cofounder and CEO Alakh Pandey also said that the company plans to scale its presence in South India for its “next leg of growth”. The edtech major plans to deploy an online-first playbook, instead of offline, to carve a niche in the five Southern states that have a total addressable market (TAM) of 1.
paragraph5: 5 Cr students. The key lever for the company in the region will be AI-powered translation, which will look to make batches available in 12 Indic languages with the same “star teachers” and no incremental academic cost. As for its outlook, the edtech company maintained a 30% consolidated revenue growth guidance. The management also said that it is targeting 100% EBITDA growth at group-level and near break-even for the offline business in the ongoing fiscal year. Separately, the company’s board also approved a proposal to acquire an additional 12.25% stake in Utkarsh Classes for ₹2.6 Lakh. This is part of PW’s multi-tranche acquisition plan to acquire the startup as detailed in its November 2025 prospectus. Once the deal goes through, PW’s stake in Utkarsh Classes will increase to 87.75% from 75.5% currently. As part of this, the board approved the fourth tranche of investment, through which the listed company will acquire 25,599 equity shares. PhysicsWallah’s board also gave its nod to replace the PAT-linked valuation mechanism, previously underlined in the agreement for the fourth tranche, with a mutually agreed fixed purchase consideration.

title: NPCI Expands Beyond Payments With AI, Blockchain-Focused Subsidiary
title_bn: এনপিসিআই এআই, ব্লকচেইন-কেন্দ্রিক শাখা সহ অর্থ প্রদানের বাইরেও সম্প্রসারণ করে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has set up a wholly owned subsidiary, NPCI Tech Solutions Ltd (NTSL), to…
paragraph1: SUMMARYNPCI has established NPCI Tech Solutions Ltd (NTSL), a wholly owned technology subsidiary, and appointed Vishal Kanvaty its MD & CEO. The new entity will build capabilities beyond NPCI’s core payments mandate, focusing on AI, blockchain, digital financial infrastructure, and global capability centre services. NTSL will also provide technology services for eKYC Setu, the Unified Ticketing Platform, and other digital public infrastructure programmes. The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has set up a wholly owned subsidiary, NPCI Tech Solutions Ltd (NTSL), to build capabilities in AI, blockchain, and digital financial infrastructure beyond its core payments mandate. The retail payments operator has appointed Vishal Kanvaty, who has been associated with NPCI for nearly a decade, as the subsidiary’s MD and CEO. NPCI said NTSL will serve as the group’s technology and innovation arm.
paragraph2: Its remit will also include global capability centre (GCC) services and technology services for eKYC Setu, the Unified Ticketing Platform (UTP), and other digital public infrastructure (DPI) programmes. According to NPCI, Kanvaty has led the development and commercialisation of several platforms that now fall within NTSL’s focus areas. NPCI MD & CEO Dilip Asbe said advances in AI and other emerging technologies are opening up opportunities across digital infrastructure and financial services. The subsidiary has been established to pursue these opportunities and strengthen the group’s technology capabilities, he added. NPCI did not disclose the subsidiary’s investment outlay, revenue targets, customer pipeline, or timelines for rolling out new services. NPCI’s Emerging Technology Push The formation follows a series of technology initiatives by NPCI.
paragraph3: At the Global Fintech Fest in September, it launched AiNxt and AtOM, platforms aimed at helping enterprises build AI agents and automate workflows across the payments ecosystem. AiNxt enables enterprises to build, test, and deploy custom AI agents, while AtOM is designed to handle integration, change management, and partner onboarding across UPI, with digitally signed interactions providing audit trails. NPCI’s work in emerging technologies also includes a multi-year research partnership with IISc, announced in March 2024, covering AI and blockchain. The collaboration envisaged developing models and software prototypes, alongside workshops and training programmes. On the payments side, NPCI demonstrated an agentic AI framework for UPI at GFF 2025. The demonstration showed how user-authorised AI assistants could discover products, place orders, and complete payments within a single conversational flow.
paragraph4: The new technology arm joins NPCI’s existing subsidiaries focused on international payments, bill payments, and BHIM. With NTSL, the group now has four wholly owned subsidiaries: NPCI International Payments Ltd (NIPL), NPCI Bharat BillPay Ltd (NBBL), NPCI BHIM Services Ltd (NBSL), and NTSL. The expansion comes alongside continued growth in its flagship payments network. UPI processed a record 25.47 Bn transactions in October, up 5.8% MoM, while transaction value increased 7.
paragraph5: 4% to ₹31.53 Lakh Cr. Average daily transaction value crossed ₹1 Lakh Cr for the first time. This came ahead of the proposed introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) charges on select UPI payments. NPCI deferred the rollout, originally scheduled for October 15, until after Diwali, with a revised implementation date yet to be announced.

title: This upcoming Google Photos tool could let you lean into that grainy, film camera look
title_bn: এই আসন্ন গুগল ফটো টুল আপনাকে সেই ধানাক্ত, ফিল্ম ক্যামেরা চেহারাতে ঝুঁকতে দেবে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The Photos app is developing four new customizable effects in the image editing interface.
paragraph1: Joe Maring / Android AuthorityAdd Android Authority on Google: TL;DR Google Photos is working on brand-new tools for the Adjust menu in its image editing interface. We have uncovered four new effects, namely Light leaks, Grain, Halation, and Noise, in a recent version of the Photos app. All these under-development effects also get sliders to let users manually adjust their intensity. Google Photos currently offers an extensive set of image editing tools, letting you make granular edits to your photos without opening another app. It now looks like the Google Photos team is developing a few more editing tools, specifically within the Adjust menu in the editing interface.
paragraph2: You’re reading an Authority Insights story. Authority Insights brings you all the latest exclusive reports, app teardowns, leaks, and in-depth tech coverage from the Android Authority team that you won’t find anywhere else.In version 8.0 of Google Photos, we activated four new options in the Adjust menu from the image editor interface, namely Light leaks, Grain, Halation, and Noise. Here’s a look at where all four options will live:AssembleDebug / Android AuthorityWe found that all four editing tools in the Adjust menu work as intended.
paragraph3: They also include sliders to adjust the intensity of the effects (0 to 100), much like some other tools in the app.First up, we’re looking at Light leaks, which adds an orange/red effect around the edges of an image, resembling light entering a camera. Google Photos could provide six options under Light leaks, each labeled in Roman numerals. Users should be able to control the visibility of these effects, with the slider highlighting the Light leaks effect currently in use.Next, we’re looking at Grain, which mimics the effects seen on analog cameras for that old-fashioned look.
paragraph4: Unlike Light leaks, however, Grain, Halation, and Noise don’t offer additional preset options.Halation adds a warm, reddish hue around bright areas of an image, which is another callback to traditional film-based cameras. Lastly, Noise brings variations in color and brightness to replicate an image captured with high ISO settings, with the onboard slider letting you tweak how much of the effect is visible.Since these effects in the Adjust menu worked normally during our testing, one might think they’re not far from an official rollout. That said, this is still an early discovery, and it’s too soon to say whether these new effects will see the light of day in the Photos app.
paragraph5: ⚠️ An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release.

title: AI moves beyond recommendations to reshape entire shopping experience on e-commerce apps: Report
title_bn: ই-কমার্স অ্যাপে সমস্ত শপিংয়ের অভিজ্ঞতা পুনরায় গঠনের জন্য এআই সুপারিশের বাইরে চলে যায়ঃ রিপোর্ট
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the way e-commerce applications personalise the shopping experience, moving beyond conventional product recommendations to potentially influence the entire interface customers see when they open an app, ac
paragraph1: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the way e-commerce applications personalise the shopping experience, moving beyond conventional product recommendations to potentially influence the entire interface customers see when they open an app, according to an industry report by AppMaker.AI moves beyond recommendations to reshape entire shopping experience on e-commerce apps: Report New Delhi [India], November 4 (ANI): Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the way e-commerce applications personalise the shopping experience, moving beyond conventional product recommendations to potentially influence the entire interface customers see when they open an app, according to an industry report by AppMaker.The report highlighted that most mobile shopping applications currently display similar homepages to visitors, with personalised recommendations generally appearing as customers browse products. However, the emerging approach involves using customers' previous activities and shopping behaviour to customise the content and layout of an application right from the beginning of a shopping session.
paragraph2: “AI is starting to push that personalization earlier: into what a shopper sees the moment they open the app, not just what is pushed toward them after they’ve already started browsing,” the report said.Under this approach, information such as products a customer has viewed, items left in a shopping cart and previous purchases could influence what appears on their screen. For instance, a returning customer who has abandoned a shopping cart could see different content from someone visiting the app for the first time.The report said this represents a shift from conventional personalisation, in which businesses decide which banners or recommendations to display to particular customer groups, towards experiences that can vary from one shopper to another.
paragraph3: “Personalisation strategies need to evolve from picking which banner a certain segment sees toward designing for a session that can feel and look different for every visitor,” said Atul Poharkar, CEO of AppMaker.The shift also has implications for how e-commerce applications are designed, developed and tested. According to the report, AI tools can assist with gathering requirements, writing user stories, developing ideas and translating design concepts into application components. This could reduce the time spent on repetitive development tasks, allowing developers to focus on functionality, integrations and business-specific requirements.
paragraph4: It also highlighted that AI could help businesses connect customer information, performance data and campaign tools that traditionally operate across separate systems.The report said these capabilities could help merchants investigate changes in conversion rates, forecast revenue and initiate campaigns targeting customers who have abandoned shopping carts or stopped engaging with a business.However, the report highlighted challenges in translating AI adoption into everyday business use. It cited a finding that 68 per cent of companies adopting AI agents reported that half or fewer of their employees interacted with an agent in their everyday work.
paragraph5: It also emphasised the need for reliable data and clear governance before businesses expand automated decision-making. Companies need to establish which decisions AI systems can make independently and which require human review.The report said the shift means e-commerce applications are increasingly being viewed not simply as products developed and launched once, but as systems that require continuous management and refinement.

title: Realme 17T 5G live images reveal redesigned camera module and slimmer bezels ahead of launch
title_bn: Realme 17T 5G live images reveal redesigned camera module and slimmer bezels ahead of launch
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Realme 17T 5G live images have surfaced online, revealing a redesigned rear camera module and slimmer display bezels ahead of its expected launch. The smartphone is expected to succeed the Realme 16T 5G and join the upcoming Realme 17 series as a mor
paragraph1: Realme 17T 5G live images have surfaced online, revealing a redesigned rear camera module and slimmer display bezels ahead of its expected launch. The smartphone is expected to succeed the Realme 16T 5G and join the upcoming Realme 17 series as a more affordable offering.The smartphone is expected to succeed the Realme 16T 5G.Realme appears to be preparing to expand its smartphone portfolio with the Realme 17T 5G, which is expected to succeed the Realme 16T 5G in India. The smartphone has yet to be officially unveiled, but leaked live images have given us a first look at its design. According to a report by 91Mobiles, which shared the images in collaboration with tipster Sudhanshu Ambhore, the handset will feature a redesigned rear camera module and slimmer display bezels.The Realme 17T 5G is likely to be the budget version in the Realme 17 series, with the specs of Realme 17 Pro and Realme 17 Pro+ expected to be revealed soon. The company has not announced its release date, specs or prices, but the appearance of live images indicates that the new smartphone is being developed.
paragraph2: Realme 17T 5G design revealed: What's changing?View full ImageThe Realme 17T.(91Mobiles)According to the leaked images from 91Mobiles, the Realme 17T 5G has been revealed from both the front and rear. The front also seems to carry over from the previous phone, featuring a punch-hole selfie camera. The bezels appear to be thinner, especially around the bottom edge, which may provide a more immersive viewing experience.The rear panel features a more noticeable design change. Realme seems to have kept the square shape of the camera module but shuffled its elements. The company has apparently packed the camera sensors and LED flash into two parallel, pill-shaped compartments.
paragraph3: The leaked handset is seen in black but may be available in other colours at launch.Realme 17T 5G specifications: What to expectRealme has yet to announce the specs of the upcoming smartphone. However, the Realme 16T 5G provides some clues to what users might look forward to in the Realme 16T 5G successor.For comparison, the Realme 16T 5G comes with a 6.8-inch HD+ LCD with up to 1200 nits of peak brightness and a 144Hz refresh rate. The MediaTek Dimensity 6300 processor is used to power it. The phone comes with a 50 MP rear camera and a 16 MP front camera.The smartphone also gets an 8,000 mAh battery that supports wired 45 W charging.
paragraph4: Realme may make some changes to the processor and camera hardware on the next-generation device, but that's still a possibility.Realme 17T 5G India launch and expected positioningThe Realme 17T 5G is likely to be the lowest-budget offering in the company's lineup. This suggests that it could target buyers looking for a more affordable smartphone without flagship-level specifications.However, Realme hasn't yet confirmed the device's existence, its launch date in India, or its expected price. For now, until the company officially announces it, the leaked design and expected specifications should be considered as unconfirmed information.About the AuthorPragya Singha RoyPragya is a Technology reporter with over four years of experience in digital media and content writing. She holds a Master’s degree in Journalism and has covered a wide range of stories spanning space, smartphones, gadgets, artificial intelligence, emerging technologies and the ways technology is transforming everyday life. She focuses on breaking down complex technology and science developments into clear, engaging, and reader-friendly stories, with a keen interest in emerging trends and their real-world impact.
paragraph5: Before joining her current newsroom, Pragya worked with News9Live, where she covered the technology beat extensively, reporting on smartphones, consumer technology, AI, space and science, while also contributing to video and visual content. Her experience includes breaking news, explainers, SEO-driven stories, product coverage, interviews, unboxing videos and live event reporting. She has also covered major technology and AI events, giving her experience in both newsroom and on-ground reporting. Beyond journalism, Pragya is an avid gamer and a passionate reader of fiction. She enjoys exploring immersive worlds through games and books, with a particular interest in stories that offer new perspectives, ideas, and experiences.

title: Lenskart Q2 Profit Jumps 125% YoY To ₹233 Cr, Revenue Rises 36%
title_bn: Lenskart Q2 Profit Jumps 125% YoY To ₹233 Cr, Revenue Rises 36%
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Listed eyewear company Lenskart reported a 124.7% jump in its consolidated net profit to ₹232.5 Cr in the September quarter…
paragraph1: SUMMARYLenskart reported a consolidated net profit of ₹232.5 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 124.7% YoY, while operating revenue increased 35.7% to ₹2,845 Cr. Listed eyewear company LensKart reported a 124.7% jump in its consolidated net profit to ₹232.5 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 (Q2 FY27) from ₹103.5 Cr in the year-ago period, with revenue growth outpacing the increase in expenses.
paragraph2: Operating revenue rose 35.7% to ₹2,845 Cr from ₹2,096.1 Cr in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, net profit increased 1.8% from ₹228.4 Cr in the preceding quarter, while operating revenue grew 4.8% from ₹2,714.2 Cr.
paragraph3: Including other income of ₹54.5 Cr, Lenskart’s total income stood at ₹2,899.5 Cr during the quarter, compared with ₹2,129.4 Cr a year earlier. Lenskart’s total expenses increased 31.1% to ₹2,596.8 Cr from ₹1,980.3 Cr in the year-ago quarter.
paragraph4: Lenskart’s India business reported revenue of ₹1,667.9 Cr, up 35.5% from ₹1,230.6 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Its segment profit increased to ₹208.4 Cr from ₹126.1 Cr. International revenue rose 36.
paragraph5: 5% to ₹1,201.1 Cr from ₹879.6 Cr, while segment profit more than tripled to ₹97.2 Cr from ₹31.1 Cr.

paragraph1: SUMMARYSequentially, the profit declined 29.1% from ₹49.7 Cr in the preceding quarter Operating revenue rose 15.8% to ₹131.7 Cr during the quarter from ₹113.8 Cr in Q2 FY26 but declined 5.7% sequentially The company's EBITDA increased 60.1% YoY to ₹45 Cr, while EBITDA margin expanded to 34.1% from 24.7% in Q2 FY26 MapmyIndia reported a 90.6% YoY jump in its consolidated net profit for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) to ₹35.3 Cr from ₹18.5 Cr in the year-ago period. Sequentially, the profit declined 29.1% from ₹49.7 Cr in the preceding quarter.
paragraph2: Operating revenue rose 15.8% to ₹131.7 Cr during the quarter from ₹113.8 Cr in Q2 FY26. The top line declined 5.7% sequentially from ₹139.7 Cr. Total income, including other income of ₹16.1 Cr, increased 19.1% to ₹147.9 Cr from ₹124.2 Cr in the year-ago period. The company’s EBITDA increased 60.1% YoY to ₹45 Cr, while EBITDA margin expanded to 34.1% from 24.7% in Q2 FY26.
paragraph3: PAT margin also improved to 23.8% from 14.9% in the corresponding quarter last year. For the first half of FY27 (H1 FY27), operating revenue grew 18.4% YoY to ₹271.5 Cr, while EBITDA increased 20.4% to ₹101.1 Cr. Net profit rose 32.2% to ₹85 Cr from ₹64.3 Cr in H1 FY26. Automotive, Enterprise Businesses Drive Growth Commenting on the performance, CMD Rakesh Verma said the company’s automotive business recorded 51.9% YoY growth in Q2 FY27, while its enterprise business grew 44.1%. For H1 FY27, the two verticals recorded growth of 40.4% and 16.
paragraph4: 5%, respectively. The automotive business’ performance was driven by increasing adoption of the company’s integrated map-led and IoT-led mobility solutions, Verma said. From a product perspective, map-led revenue grew 8.9% to ₹175.3 Cr in H1 FY27, while EBITDA margins for the business stood at 47.1%. IoT-led revenue increased 29.1% to ₹96.2 Cr during the period. The IoT-led business also reported a significant improvement in profitability, with EBITDA increasing to ₹18.5 Cr in H1 FY27 from ₹7.9 Cr in the corresponding period last year. The company attributed this to higher-margin solutions and operating leverage. MapmyIndia provides digital map data, geospatial software and location-based IoT products, platforms and solutions. Its offerings include mapping APIs, navigation and telematics solutions for automotive and enterprise customers. MapmyIndia Rejigs Leadership Alongside its Q2 results, MapmyIndia announced a series of leadership changes across its technology, product and business teams as it looks to expand its AI capabilities and develop new products.
paragraph5: The company appointed Abhit Kalasotra as chief technology officer (CTO), software engineering, and Nitin Sagar as chief product technology officer (CPTO) for Mappls AI, effective November 4, 2026. Kalasotra brings over 22 years of technical experience, including 12 years of building technology companies. He has previously worked with Microsoft, Nokia, Emuzed, LG and Motorola. He holds a bachelor’s degree in computer science from BITS Pilani. Sagar, meanwhile, has over 17 years of experience across location intelligence, digital payments and global travel. He previously worked at MapmyIndia between 2009 and 2015, where he led product and platform development and integrations with automotive manufacturers. The company also re-designated Rashmi Verma, previously CTO and chief human resource officer (CHRO), as chief innovation officer (CIO). In her new role, she will focus on driving innovation and accelerating the adoption of AI and emerging technologies across the group. Separately, CFO Anuj Kumar Jain has been assigned the additional responsibility of chief operating officer (COO) at Gtropy Systems Private Limited, a subsidiary of MapmyIndia. Vishal Pandey has also been appointed chief business officer (CBO) of Gtropy Systems, with both changes taking effect on November 4. The leadership changes come as MapmyIndia looks to embed AI, machine learning and neural networks across its map-led and IoT-led platforms. These applications span intelligent mapping, navigation, in-vehicle intelligence, telematics, analytics and workflow automation. Verma said the company sees long-term growth opportunities across its market and product segments, backed by its proprietary data, geospatial capabilities and IoT portfolio. Shares of MapmyIndia ended today’s trading session 4.57% higher at ₹890.20 apiece on the BSE.

title: Pine Labs Partners With Stripe To Unify Online, In-Store Payments In Singapore
title_bn: পাইন ল্যাবস স্ট্রাইপের সাথে অংশীদার হয়ে সিঙ্গাপুরে অনলাইনে, ইন-স্টোর পেমেন্ট একীভূত করবে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Listed fintech major Pine Labs has partnered with global payments infrastructure provider Stripe to launch a solution that allows eligible…
paragraph1: SUMMARYPine Labs has partnered with Stripe to launch a unified commerce solution for eligible Singapore retailers, combining online payments with card acceptance at physical stores. The offering aims to simplify payment management for retailers operating across stores and digital channels, addressing fragmented reporting and reconciliation across separate providers. The rollout begins this month, with expansion to other Southeast Asian markets planned in 2027 and access to instalment plans, loyalty-linked payments, and merchant promotions. Listed fintech major Pine Labs has partnered with global payments infrastructure provider Stripe to launch a solution that allows eligible retailers in Singapore to manage online and in-store payments through a single platform. The offering combines Stripe’s online payment capabilities with Pine Labs’ payment terminals and merchant commerce tools.
paragraph2: Participating merchants will be able to process online payments through Stripe and accept card payments at physical stores through Pine Labs’ terminals, starting this month. The companies plan to expand the offering to other Southeast Asian markets in 2027. The solution targets retailers selling through both physical stores and digital channels. Managing separate payment providers across these channels can complicate reporting and reconciliation, while adding to operational costs. Beyond payment acceptance, retailers will get access to Pine Labs’ instalment plans from multiple issuers, loyalty-linked payments, pay-by-points options, merchant-funded promotions, and digital marketing tools.
paragraph3: The companies will showcase the solution at the Singapore Fintech Festival 2026. Pine Labs’ Overseas Push The partnership builds on Pine Labs’ expansion of its merchant payments and commerce business across international markets. As of Q2 FY27, Pine Labs served 11.6 Lakh merchants, up 13% YoY, with a presence across more than 22 markets. Its offerings span merchant payments, payment orchestration, issuing, prepaid instruments, and credit infrastructure, with acquisitions helping broaden its product portfolio.
paragraph4: Pine Labs merged its Singapore holding company with its Indian entity in June 2025. It subsequently listed on the BSE and the NSE at ₹242 apiece, a 9.5% premium to its issue price. On the financial front, Pine Labs’ net profit jumped more than sixfold to ₹38.6 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹6 Cr in the year-ago quarter.
paragraph5: Operating revenue rose 24% YoY to ₹806.2 Cr. Shares of Pine Labs were trading 1.15% higher at ₹157.70 apiece on the BSE at 14:45 IST.

title: 87% of organisations face threat-related incidents, preparedness gaps persist: McKinsey
title_bn: ৮৭% সংস্থার হুমকি সম্পর্কিত ঘটনা ঘটেছে, প্রস্তুতির অভাব অব্যাহত রয়েছেঃ ম্যাককিনসি
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Around 87 per cent of organisations experienced at least one threat-related incident in the 24 months preceding a survey, but many remain inadequately prepared to deal with risks beyond conventional cybersecurity, according to a report by McKinsey &
paragraph1: Around 87 per cent of organisations experienced at least one threat-related incident in the 24 months preceding a survey, but many remain inadequately prepared to deal with risks beyond conventional cybersecurity, according to a report by McKinsey & Company.87% of organisations face threat-related incidents, preparedness gaps persist: McKinseyNew Delhi [India], November 4 (ANI): Around 87 per cent of organisations experienced at least one threat-related incident in the 24 months preceding a survey, but many remain inadequately prepared to deal with risks beyond conventional cybersecurity, according to a report by McKinsey & Company.The report found that technology infrastructure and software were the most affected areas, with 75 per cent of respondents reporting threat-related incidents involving these systems.Physical and industrial infrastructure accounted for 31 per cent of reported incidents, while economic and financial systems and supply chain ecosystems accounted for 29 per cent each.
paragraph2: The findings highlight how businesses are increasingly exposed to threats that can affect multiple systems, extending beyond conventional cyberattacks.Based on a survey conducted across organisations, sectors and geographies in the first quarter of 2026, the report pointed to a widening gap between the growing complexity of threats and organisations' ability to respond to them.McKinsey noted that traditional infrastructure, including power grids, water systems, transportation, healthcare and telecommunications, is becoming increasingly dependent on digital technologies such as data centres, cloud platforms and AI computing capacity."As these systems become more interconnected, a disruption to one technology provider or platform can cascade across physical infrastructure, supply chains, and essential services," the report stated.
paragraph3: However, organisations have developed stronger capabilities to address cybersecurity and physical security risks than other emerging threats.Around 98 per cent of surveyed organisations have established capabilities to manage cyber and information technology risks, while 77 per cent have arrangements to deal with risks involving physical and hardware infrastructure.Preparedness is considerably lower in other areas. Only 59 per cent of organisations have capabilities to manage information and psychological operations risks, while 47 per cent have arrangements to address economic and political coercion.
paragraph4: The figure falls to 32 per cent for espionage and covert operations.This gap is significant as 64 per cent of organisations consider espionage a highly relevant threat to their businesses, the report said.McKinsey highlighted that espionage and covert operations are often designed to remain undetected, making it difficult for organisations without dedicated capabilities to identify and respond to such threats.The report also flagged a lack of coordination within organisations, with responsibility for risk management often divided across departments.
paragraph5: While cybersecurity teams typically oversee digital systems, physical security, compliance and enterprise risk management are frequently handled by separate teams.It noted that budgets, capabilities and accountability often follow organisational boundaries, even as threats increasingly cut across these divisions.The report called on business leaders to identify areas where their preparedness falls short of the threats they consider relevant and align investments and collaboration accordingly.It also emphasised the need for an integrated approach to managing risks across technology and physical infrastructure, as growing interdependence between these systems increases the potential impact of disruptions.

Only 59 per cent of organisations have capabilities to manage information and psychological operations risks, while 47 per cent have arrangements to address economic and political coercion.

title: Jio In Talks With US-Based Comcast, Charter To License Broadband Technology: Report
title_bn: ব্রডব্যান্ড প্রযুক্তির লাইসেন্স দেওয়ার জন্য মার্কিন কমকাস্টের সঙ্গে আলোচনায় জিও
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Recently listed Jio Platforms has held discussions with US cable operators Comcast and Charter Communications about licensing its wireless broadband…
paragraph1: SUMMARYJio Platforms is in discussions with US cable operators Comcast and Charter Communications to license its UBR technology in exchange for potential equity stakes The talks come as Jio pushes to expand its wireless broadband technology overseas through partnerships, with the company targeting 10-15 global partners Jio's discussions with South Africa's MTN Group fell through over valuation and licensing issues, while the company recently made its stock market debut at a 21.36% premium to its IPO price Recently listed Jio Platforms has held discussions with US cable operators Comcast and Charter Communications about licensing its wireless broadband technology in exchange for potential equity stakes. According to a Reuters report, the discussions are part of the Reliance Industries-controlled company’s overseas expansion plans, centred on selling its proprietary unlicensed band radio (UBR) technology to foreign operators rather than building networks abroad. Jio is targeting 10-15 global partners for the technology, which delivers high-speed internet to buildings without requiring cable connections to individual homes. However, there is no timeline for reaching an agreement with any of the companies it has approached, the report said. Jio also held discussions with South Africa’s MTN Group, but the talks fell through after the two sides failed to agree on valuation and certain licensing issues.
paragraph2: The report cited one of the sources as saying that MTN could not persuade Jio to invest at a valuation acceptable to the Indian company. Inc42 has reached out to Jio Platforms, Comcast and Charter Communications for comments on the development. The story will be updated on receiving their responses. Jio Eyes Overseas Markets For UBR Technology Jio’s UBR platform operates on free, unlicensed Wi-Fi frequencies. It uses transmitters installed on nearby towers or rooftops to beam internet to receivers fitted on buildings. The technology could help operators deliver broadband without laying cables to individual homes or relying on licensed mobile spectrum.
paragraph3: Reliance has described it as a global first. A partnership with Comcast or Charter could give Jio access to the US residential broadband market, where cable operators are facing growing competition from fibre and fixed wireless services. Comcast had around 28.3 Mn residential broadband customers at the end of September, while Charter had approximately 29.4 Mn internet customers in June. Both companies have been losing customers to fixed wireless and fibre providers.
paragraph4: Last month, Jio made its stock market debut following a $3.2 Bn IPO, listing at a 21.36% premium to the issue price of ₹1,119 on BSE and NSE. Jio Platforms reported a net profit of ₹8,387 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 13.7% from ₹7,375 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, profit rose 8% from ₹7,764 Cr.
paragraph5: During its earnings call, Jio Platforms MD Akash Ambani said the company wanted to take UBR to both developed and developing markets but would be selective about where it expands. “We want to be a technology-led business there,” he said, highlighting the potential of the US market. Jio added 9.1 Mn customers on a net basis during the quarter, taking its subscriber base to 542.4 Mn. It also reported 300 Mn 5G subscribers.

The technology could help operators deliver broadband without laying cables to individual homes or relying on licensed mobile spectrum.
bangla_paragraph3: Reliance has described it as a global first. A partnership with Comcast or Charter could give Jio access to the US residential broadband market, where cable operators are facing growing competition from fibre and fixed wireless services. Comcast had around 28.3 Mn residential broadband customers at the end of September, while Charter had approximately 29.4 Mn internet customers in June. Both companies have been losing customers to fixed wireless and fibre providers.
bangla_paragraph4: Last month, Jio made its stock market debut following a $3.2 Bn IPO, listing at a 21.36% premium to the issue price of ₹1,119 on BSE and NSE. Jio Platforms reported a net profit of ₹8,387 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 13.7% from ₹7,375 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, profit rose 8% from ₹7,764 Cr.
bangla_paragraph5: During its earnings call, Jio Platforms MD Akash Ambani said the company wanted to take UBR to both developed and developing markets but would be selective about where it expands. “We want to be a technology-led business there,” he said, highlighting the potential of the US market. Jio added 9.1 Mn customers on a net basis during the quarter, taking its subscriber base to 542.4 Mn. It also reported 300 Mn 5G subscribers.

paragraph1: SUMMARYFreshworks reported a consolidated net profit of $18.3 Mn in Q3 2026 against a $4.7 Mn loss a year earlier, while revenue increased 14% to $245.4 Mn Higher revenue and lower operating expenses helped Freshworks sustain GAAP profitability, while its push towards larger customers gained traction Freshworks crossed $1 Bn in annual recurring revenue after the quarter ended, ahead of its year-end target Nasdaq-listed SaaS company Freshworks swung to a consolidated net profit of $18.3 Mn in the third quarter of 2026 (Q3 2026) from a $4.7 Mn loss a year earlier, helped by higher revenue and lower operating expenses. Revenue rose 14% to $245.4 Mn from $215.1 Mn in the corresponding quarter last year. Sequentially, revenue increased 3.
paragraph2: 4% from $237.4 Mn, while net profit rose from $3.2 Mn. The company’s operating expenses declined 4.4% to $181.2 Mn from $189.6 Mn. General and administrative expenses fell to $38.2 Mn from $47.1 Mn, while stock-based compensation dropped to $38.
paragraph3: 8 Mn from $48.5 Mn. Enterprise Push Gains Traction CEO Dennis Woodside said Freshworks’ strategy of targeting larger customers supported its quarterly performance. New deals involving multiple employee experience products increased more than 35%, while partners participated in more than half of its new business, he said. The number of customers contributing over $100,000 in annual recurring revenue (ARR) increased 25% to 1,821. Customers generating more than $50,000 in ARR grew 18% to 4,257. Freshworks also crossed $1 Bn in ARR after the quarter ended, ahead of its earlier year-end target. However, its net dollar retention (NDR) rate remained unchanged sequentially at 104%, down from 105% a year earlier. NDR measures changes in revenue from existing customers, accounting for upgrades, cross-sells, renewals, and customer churn. New customers during the quarter included Tata Technologies, Texas Christian University, Unilabs (UK), and Jose Cuervo.
paragraph4: Freshworks has been increasingly positioning itself as an AI-powered service operations platform spanning customer experience, employee experience, and IT service management. It forecast full-year revenue of $965 Mn-$966 Mn implying about 15% growth. This narrows its earlier guidance of $963.5 Mn-$966.5 Mn. Founded in 2010 by Girish Mathrubootham and Shan Krishnasamy, Freshworks offers cloud-based software for customer support, sales automation, and IT service management. It became the first Indian SaaS company to list on Nasdaq in September 2021.
paragraph5: Under Woodside, who succeeded Mathrubootham as CEO in 2024, the company has sharpened its focus on AI-led enterprise software. In May 2026, Freshworks announced plans to cut approximately 500 jobs, or 11% of its workforce, to realign operations around its growth priorities and accelerate its AI push. It has also expanded through acquisitions, buying IT incident management platform FireHydrant for $88.7 Mn in cash in January to strengthen its IT service and operations portfolio. More recently, Freshworks acquired Israel-based AI startup Robusta Dev for an undisclosed amount. It plans to integrate Robusta’s AI-powered outage investigation and corrective recommendations into Freshservice, complementing FireHydrant’s incident response tools.

title: Peppermint Robotics Bags ₹100 Cr To Scale Its Industrial Robotics Bet
title_bn: শিল্প রোবোটিক্সের জন্য ১০০ কোটি টাকা বরাদ্দ পেপারমিন্ট রোবট ব্যাগ
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Keeping hospital corridors clean or moving goods across factory floors involves repetitive, physically demanding work. For facility management companies, finding…
paragraph1: SUMMARYPeppermint Robotics has raised ₹100 Cr in a Pre-Series B round comprising primary and secondary transactions The startup is expanding from floor-cleaning robots into material handling and cleanroom automation, targeting more applications across factories, warehouses, and pharmaceutical facilities Peppermint plans to expand its cleaning and material-handling portfolio with new models and upgrades over the next 12-15 months, followed by outdoor cleaning robots by 2028 Keeping hospital corridors clean or moving goods across factory floors involves repetitive, physically demanding work. For facility management companies, finding people to carry out these tasks is becoming harder. This workforce gap is the opportunity behind Peppermint Robotics. Founded in 2019 and incubated at SINE, IIT Bombay, the Pune-based startup builds autonomous robots that scrub floors and move materials across commercial and industrial facilities. Now, it has raised ₹100 Cr (about $10.5 Mn) in a Pre-Series B round to expand manufacturing, develop new robots, and strengthen its US and European businesses. Led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners, with participation from Asiana Fund, the round comprised primary capital and secondary share transactions.
paragraph2: Founder Runal Dahiwade told Inc42 that the bulk of the investment was primary capital. The startup previously raised ₹34 Cr in a Series A round in April 2025. Moving Beyond Floor Cleaning Featured in Inc42’s June 2020 edition of ‘30 Startups To Watch’, Peppermint began with a floor-cleaning and sanitising robot. Its portfolio now spans scrubber-dryers, vacuuming and mopping robots, three material-handling models, and automated docking stations. The startup says its cleanroom scrubber-dryer has passed qualification testing in an EU GMP Grade C cleanroom. Such controlled environments require strict limits on contamination, creating a specialised application beyond routine cleaning. Dahiwade also claimed Peppermint is the world’s first cleanroom robotics company.
paragraph3: Over the next 12-15 months, Peppermint plans smaller and larger cleaning and material-handling robots, alongside upgrades. Outdoor cleaning robots are planned by 2028. Its proprietary Peppermint OS powers navigation, while computer vision and LiDAR help machines map spaces and avoid obstacles. Customers can monitor operations through a cloud dashboard and mobile apps. Selling Machines And Support Peppermint sells robots primarily to facility management companies, earning additional revenue from spare parts, annual maintenance contracts, and software and hardware upgrades from the second year. An average robot costs around ₹20 Lakh in India. US prices range from $35,000 to $40,000, depending on installation and other costs, Dahiwade said.
paragraph4: Its operating revenue rose from ₹2.71 Cr in FY23 to ₹6.26 Cr in FY24 and ₹21 Cr in FY25. The founder said revenue doubled last year and grew nearly sixfold between FY24 and FY26. The US contributes nearly half its revenue, India close to 30%, and other markets the remainder. Peppermint is planning to set up an assembly line in North America, adding to its Pune manufacturing and R&D base. It competes with China’s Gausium and Singapore’s LionsBot.
paragraph5: Dahiwade claimed Peppermint commands over 65% of India’s floor-cleaning robotics market. Inc42 Take: Can Peppermint Scale Without Stretching Its Service Network? Selling through facility management companies offers a route to deployments across multiple customer locations. Expanding into material handling and cleanrooms could widen this opportunity. The bigger test is servicing these machines across markets while funding a broader portfolio. According to Peppermint, its core business has operated profitably for several quarters, but R&D and international expansion have kept the company loss-making overall. Converting fresh capital into reliable deployments and repeat business will matter more than portfolio breadth alone.

title: Inside The New Wave Of Private AI
title_bn: Inside The New Wave Of Private AI
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Can you trust a stranger with your login credentials, personal information, or private conversations? Of course not! Yet, we are…
paragraph1: Can you trust a stranger with your login credentials, personal information, or private conversations? Of course not! Yet, we are increasingly trusting AI assistants with precisely this kind of information. The rationale is simple: The more these assistants know about us, the more useful they become. However, this convenience comes with an uncomfortable question: Can we trust them? The stakes are even higher for businesses, as AI assistants increasingly handle proprietary information, financial records and confidential legal documents. This growing tension has created an opening for privacy-focused AI products. In October, Eternal announced Dark.ai, a privacy-focused AI assistant built around open-weight models and positioned around end-to-end encryption. Globally, products such as Brave Leo, Duck.ai and Proton Lumo are also attempting to address growing concerns over how AI systems handle sensitive information. So, can it become the next big competitive advantage in AI? And, more importantly, what will it take for startups to turn that promise into a sustainable business? Let’s explore in The AI Shift… The Privacy Trade-Off The more an AI assistant knows, the better it can do its job.
paragraph2: But there is a catch. To deliver useful answers, it may need access to information that users and businesses would rather keep private. Take a legal AI assistant, for instance. It may need to go through confidential case files to help lawyers with research. Similarly, an AI platform in financial services may need access to loan histories, transaction records and customer communications. This puts AI startups in a tricky position. Without enough data and context, AI products may not be useful. On the flip side, how can these assistants be trusted if there is no guarantee that sensitive information will be handled safely. Saakar Yadav, founder of legal research and workflow platform Lexlegis.ai, has seen this challenge firsthand. He said some organisations want to use AI to work with confidential legal documents but are unwilling to let that information leave their systems. For such customers, running AI locally on their own computers, even without an internet connection, could offer a solution. The challenge is that there is no single way to make AI private. Some companies keep data on users’ devices, while others hide identifying details, encrypt conversations or restrict who can access the information.
paragraph3: Each approach addresses a different risk, and what works for one AI product may not be enough for another. For instance, AI-powered consumer assistant SuperLiving is working on protecting user information by masking conversations so that individual users cannot be easily identified. Cofounder Manavdeep Singh Grover said that the company is also working towards introducing encryption to strengthen its privacy safeguards. However, masking alone cannot solve every privacy concern. Companies also need to consider where conversations are stored, who can access them and how the information is processed. From Encrypted Chats To AI That Stays Offline AI companies are approaching privacy through different technical choices, rather than relying on a single definition of a private assistant. Brave Leo, from privacy-focused browser company Brave, has outlined protections that include encrypted conversations and confidential computing for supported inference. Duck.ai, from search engine DuckDuckGo, says it removes identifying information from requests before sending them to model providers. Proton Lumo, from privacy-focused technology company Proton, said it does not keep logs of conversations and does not use chats to train models without explicit permission. Apple’s Private Cloud Compute takes another approach, using dedicated servers designed to process requests without retaining user data after they are handled. Apple has also said that independent researchers can inspect the system’s security properties. The stakes are particularly high in financial services, where AI systems may need access to transaction histories, repayment behaviour and investment preferences to assist customers with financial decisions. But access to this information should not translate into unrestricted permission to use it.
paragraph4: Ashutosh Prakash Singh, cofounder and CEO at RevRag.ai, which works on AI solutions, argues that financial institutions need clear boundaries around what an in-app AI agent can access and infer, how long information is retained, and whether it can be used to train or improve models. He believes stronger data protection will increasingly become a business necessity rather than just a compliance requirement. Financial institutions will assess AI not only on efficiency and cost, but also on governance, traceability and accountability. Losing customer confidence over how financial information is used can be as damaging as a data breach. As AI becomes more deeply embedded in financial services, trust will be central to whether customers are willing to use it. This makes choosing architecture important. Some workflows may be served by masking and access controls, while others may require stricter retention policies, secure deployment environments or additional safeguards around where data is processed. RECOMMENDED FOR yOU The opportunity for startups is therefore not simply to market an AI assistant as private but to build products whose privacy protections match the sensitivity of the work they are designed to handle. Privacy As A Business Opportunity Privacy can influence purchasing decisions, but it may not be enough to sustain an AI business on its own. Products still need to solve a meaningful problem and deliver an experience that customers are willing to pay for. Kushal Bhagia, founding partner at All In Capital, believes privacy can be a strong differentiator when the underlying product is already compelling. “Privacy becomes the reason someone chooses one product over another when the underlying utility is already compelling,” he said. The distinction matters because not every customer will pay a premium for stronger privacy.
paragraph5: A business using AI for routine internal tasks may have different requirements from one processing financial records, proprietary research or confidential customer information. For the latter, safeguards may be a basic condition for adoption rather than an optional add-on. There are several possible opportunities here, including private AI infrastructure, secure deployment, data governance tools and specialised assistants built for sensitive workflows. But these products also bring costs. Security engineering, encryption, infrastructure and compliance can make development and deployment more expensive. According to SuperLiving’s Grover, the company is working towards compliance with India’s Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) framework, including considerations around data retention, encryption and the information shared with large language models. The commercial challenge is to make such safeguards credible without making the product too expensive or cumbersome. Customers need to understand what protections are in place, how those protections work and what risks remain. Yet, we are increasingly trusting AI assistants with precisely this kind of information. The rationale is simple: The more these assistants know about us, the more useful they become. However, this convenience comes with an uncomfortable question: Can we trust them? It may need to go through confidential case files to help lawyers with research. Similarly, an AI platform in financial services may need access to loan histories, transaction records and customer communications. This puts AI startups in a tricky position. Without enough data and context, AI products may not be useful. On the flip side, how can these assistants be trusted if there is no guarantee that sensitive information will be handled safely. Saakar Yadav, founder of legal research and workflow platform Lexlegis.ai, has seen this challenge firsthand. He said some organisations want to use AI to work with confidential legal documents but are unwilling to let that information leave their systems. For such customers, running AI locally on their own computers, even without an internet connection, could offer a solution. The challenge is that there is no single way to make AI private. Some companies keep data on users’ devices, while others hide identifying details, encrypt conversations or restrict who can access the information.

For instance, AI-powered consumer assistant SuperLiving is working on protecting user information by masking conversations so that individual users cannot be easily identified. Cofounder Manavdeep Singh Grover said that the company is also working towards introducing encryption to strengthen its privacy safeguards. However, masking alone cannot solve every privacy concern. Companies also need to consider where conversations are stored, who can access them and how the information is processed. Duck.ai, from search engine DuckDuckGo, says it removes identifying information from requests before sending them to model providers. Proton Lumo, from privacy-focused technology company Proton, said it does not keep logs of conversations and does not use chats to train models without explicit permission. Apple’s Private Cloud Compute takes another approach, using dedicated servers designed to process requests without retaining user data after they are handled. Apple has also said that independent researchers can inspect the system’s security properties. The stakes are particularly high in financial services, where AI systems may need access to transaction histories, repayment behaviour and investment preferences to assist customers with financial decisions. But access to this information should not translate into unrestricted permission to use it.
bangla_paragraph4: Ashutosh Prakash Singh, cofounder and CEO at RevRag.ai, which works on AI solutions, argues that financial institutions need clear boundaries around what an in-app AI agent can access and infer, how long information is retained, and whether it can be used to train or improve models. He believes stronger data protection will increasingly become a business necessity rather than just a compliance requirement. Financial institutions will assess AI not only on efficiency and cost, but also on governance, traceability and accountability. Losing customer confidence over how financial information is used can be as damaging as a data breach. title: EloElo Group Bags $80 Mn From NBCUniversal, Others To Take Its Microdrama Biz Global
title_bn: EloElo Group Bags $80 Mn From NBCUniversal, Others To Take Its Microdrama Biz Global
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Microdrama platform Story TV’s parent EloElo Group has raised $80 Mn (nearly ₹756 Cr) in a Series C funding round…
paragraph1: SUMMARYBesides Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal, the round also saw participation from MIT Investment, Play Ventures, Kalaari Capital, Waterbridge Ventures, among others The company will use the fresh capital to invest in premium original content across Indian languages, expand Story TV to international markets and strengthen its AI capabilities Founded in 2020, EloElo Group operates four products – Story TV (microdrama platform), Master (microlearning platform) Dolphin AI (an AI-powered creative suite) and AI agent Voxy Microdrama platform Story TV’s parent EloElo Group has raised $80 Mn (nearly ₹756 Cr) in a Series C funding round led by global media and entertainment giant NBCUniversal and Hornbill Capital. The round also saw participation from MIT Investment Co. and existing backers including Play Ventures, Kalaari Capital, Waterbridge Ventures and Griffin Gaming Partners, among others. The company will use the fresh capital to invest in premium original content across Indian languages, expand Story TV to international markets and strengthen its AI capabilities through Dolphin AI, its recently launched AI creative suite.
paragraph2: Founded in 2020 by former Flipkart executive Saurabh Pandey, EloElo Group operates four products — Story TV (microdrama platform), Master (microlearning platform) Dolphin AI (an AI-powered creative suite) and Voxy AI (an AI companion agent). Story TV remains the company’s largest product, with over 5,000 microdramas across six languages. Across its portfolio of apps, EloElo Group claims to have over 40 Mn monthly active users and more than 300 Mn installs. Speaking to Inc42, Pandey said the company plans to deepen its premium content slate by working with established production studios and experimenting with AI-generated and hybrid microdramas.
paragraph3: It currently works with over 90 production studios, including Indian production house Balaji Telefilms. The company also plans to take Story TV to international markets. Pandey further said the company would identify markets and work with local talent pools as part of the expansion. Another focus area will be Dolphin AI, which allows users to generate videos, images and longer-form AI content, including films.
paragraph4: EloElo currently has a team of around 200 people, of which 8-10 work on Dolphin AI. The fresh capital will support hiring across data science, generative AI, engineering and computer infrastructure teams. Pandey said EloElo’s strategy is to control three layers of the entertainment value chain: intellectual property, AI-powered production infrastructure and content distribution. With the latest fundraise, EloElo Group has raised $130 Mn to date.
paragraph5: The funding comes amid growing interest in the microdrama format. According to a report, the global microdrama industry is expected to generate $14 Bn in revenue by the end of 2026..

title: Dell 14S laptop debuts in India with Intel Core 5, Core 7 processors: Price, features, specifications
title_bn: Dell 14S laptop debuts in India with Intel Core 5, Core 7 processors: Price, features, specifications
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Dell has launched the 14S laptop in India at a starting price of ₹79,990, with four colour options. It features Intel Series 3 Core 5 and Core 7 processors, up to 16GB of RAM, 1TB of storage and a display with up to a 120Hz refresh rate.
paragraph1: Dell has launched the 14S laptop in India at a starting price of ₹79,990, with four colour options. It features Intel Series 3 Core 5 and Core 7 processors, up to 16GB of RAM, 1TB of storage and a display with up to a 120Hz refresh rate.Dell has launched the 14S laptop in India.Dell has introduced the new Dell 14S laptop with its lightweight design and various colours in India to add more diversity to its notebook offerings. Announced in India on 4 November, the laptop targets younger consumers looking for a portable device with performance-focused features. It starts at ₹79,990 and comes in four colour options.The Dell 14S has an aluminium body and the Intel Series 3 CPUs and up to 16GB RAM. It also has two display modes – a 120Hz panel with higher-end variants.
paragraph2: Dell says it can get up to 21 hours of video streaming per charge.Dell 14S design and displayThe Dell 14S has an aluminium chassis that is 13.5mm thick and 1.15kg. It features a 180-degree hinge, one-touch lid opening and a backlit keyboard. The Dell laptop comes in four colours – Linen, Dusty Rose, Washed Denim and Velvet Green.On the display side, the buyer can choose between a 2K IPS panel with a 60Hz refresh rate and 300-nit brightness or a higher-end 2.8K panel with a 120Hz refresh rate and 450-nit brightness.
paragraph3: The displays are 16:10 in aspect ratio.There are also stereo speakers with Dolby Atmos support.Dell 14S processor, RAM and batteryThe Dell 14S features Intel Series 3 processors (Core 5 and Core 7). It is also capable of delivering up to 17 TOPS of NPU performance for on-device AI workloads.The basic variant has 8GB of LPDDR5X RAM and 256GB of storage. More expensive models have up to 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage.The laptop offers up to 21 hours of battery life when streaming video, according to Dell. However, the company has not disclosed its charging speeds.
paragraph4: The Dell 14S has two USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 ports for connectivity, as well as an HDMI port and a universal audio jack. It also has Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.4 capabilities. There are other features, such as support for Windows Hello and a 2 MP Full HD webcam.Dell 14S price and availability in IndiaThe Dell 14S starts at ₹79,990 in India. It can be purchased from Dell's official website and authorized retail partners.Dell's India launch announcement states that customers will also be eligible for a discount of up to ₹10,000 through eligible bank offers, subject to applicable terms & conditions.

She holds a Master’s degree in Journalism and has covered a wide range of stories spanning space, smartphones, gadgets, artificial intelligence, emerging technologies and the ways technology is transforming everyday life. She focuses on breaking down complex technology and science developments into clear, engaging, and reader-friendly stories, with a keen interest in emerging trends and their real-world impact. Her experience includes breaking news, explainers, SEO-driven stories, product coverage, interviews, unboxing videos and live event reporting. She has also covered major technology and AI events, giving her experience in both newsroom and on-ground reporting. Beyond journalism, Pragya is an avid gamer and a passionate reader of fiction. She enjoys exploring immersive worlds through games and books, with a particular interest in stories that offer new perspectives, ideas, and experiences.
